start: ^Narrator: The office is small and lived-in. A framed photo faces the chair. On the screen, a folder is still open: "GHOST -- Hospital Infrastructure Assessment".
^Narrator: A man is sitting in the dark with his coat on, as if he has been about to leave for hours and hasn't managed it. He doesn't startle.
^Danny Foster: You're not one of ours. I'd know you.

b: ^Danny Foster: You've seen it. The hospital files.
^Danny Foster: You're here about the hospital. Aren't you.

start: ^SAFETYNET. I'm investigating the St. Catherine's attack.
^She lied to you about the client, didn't she.
reveal: ^Danny Foster: I didn't know. You have to believe that. She told me it was a security-awareness client. That's what the paperwork says because that's what she told me to write.
^Danny Foster: And then I saw the news, and I knew exactly what I'd handed her.
guilt: ^Danny Foster: *voice cracks* I know. I know what my map was for.
^Danny Foster: I read every article. I could tell you the ward layout from memory because I drew it. I keep thinking if I'd asked one more question --
^Danny Foster: But I didn't. I did good, thorough work, and I gave it to her, and she sold it.
sympathy: ^Danny Foster: Security-awareness training at a healthcare client. Her exact words. I even believed the invoice.
^Danny Foster: I did the work. Careful work. And then the ransomware ran on the exact FTP box I'd flagged, and I understood what careful had bought.
the_question: ^Danny Foster: When I worked it out, I went to her. She told me I was paranoid. Then she gave me a raise and called me essential.
^Danny Foster: She was buying my silence and I was letting her. The alternative is this.
^Danny Foster: A stranger in my office at night, and me trying to explain I'm not what the map makes me look like.
^Come in and testify. You were deceived. I'll put that in the report myself.
^You drew the map, took the money, stayed quiet. You'll answer for it.
^This isn't my call. You know what you did. Decide it yourself.
protect: ^Sterling goes down for her part. You don't have to. But you tell them everything.

c-0: ^Narrator: He reaches for his phone with a hand that isn't quite steady, and for the first time all night he looks like a man who might sleep.

expose: ^Danny Foster: *quietly* You're not wrong. That's the worst of it. You're not wrong.
^I'm logging it all -- recon, emails, the raise. Cooperating helps you. Nothing erases it.

c-0: ^Danny Foster: Then I'll cooperate. For what it's worth. Just... in whatever you write, say I didn't know at the start. Please.
^Narrator: He doesn't argue. Somewhere in the last few months he stopped believing he'd get to.

leave: ^Danny Foster: That's almost worse. At least a decision made for me isn't mine.
^Yours is the only one that'll hold. Make it.

c-0: ^Narrator: You leave him with the photo, the open folder, and the phone. Whatever he does with the three of them, he does alone.

b: ^Danny Foster: I'm still here. I said I would be.

after_choice: ^Danny's on the phone to SAFETYNET. Leave him to it.
^Danny's still staring at the phone. Leave him.
